title: Amazon Leo Surpasses 375 Satellites, Enough for Initial Commercial Service in 2026
detail: A United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket launched 29 more Amazon Leo satellites from Florida on July 2, 2026 — the constellation's 14th mission — bringing the total in orbit to more than 375, the third-largest constellation currently flying. Amazon said it now has enough satellites in orbit to begin 'initial service' of its Leo internet-from-space network later in 2026. Under its FCC license, Amazon must launch half of its first-generation constellation by July 30, 2026, though the FCC waived that deadline in June 2026 following an Amazon request for an extension. Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) is already running enterprise beta service with carrier partners including Verizon, AT&T, Vodafone, and Vodacom.

title: South Africa Launches State-Backed BrainSAT Satellite Communications Company
detail: South Africa launched BrainSAT Satellite Services on July 2, 2026, a state-backed satellite communications company formed in partnership with UAE-based Space42, stemming from a Memorandum of Understanding signed during an April 2024 state visit to Dubai. Deputy President Paul Mashatile officially inaugurated the company in Johannesburg. BrainSAT will offer Space42's YahClick Ka-band high-throughput satellite broadband and Thuraya mobile satellite services, targeting underserved rural areas and sectors including mining, agriculture, maritime operations, and emergency response, as part of South Africa's National Satellite Communication Strategy. The launch comes as South Africa's roughly 13 million still-offline citizens await a decision on Starlink's stalled license application, which remains blocked over BEE ownership requirements.
